summary.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 11% YoY to INR3,193 crore, but PBDIT fell to INR400 crore from INR426 crore on sugar cost pressure.
summary.overview: DCM Shriram's Q4 FY26 net revenue (net of excise) grew 11% YoY to INR3,193 crore, while PBDIT declined to INR400 crore from INR426 crore. Chemicals revenue rose 32% and Vinyl PBDIT jumped 68%, but Sugar and ethanol PBDIT fell 18% on higher cane prices and Fenesta's margin was diluted by costs. FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR13,538 crore and PBDIT rose 15% to INR1,694 crore, with net debt at INR1,767 crore and ROCE at 13%. Management flagged high PVC price volatility and an unresolved ethanol allocation problem as the main near-term concerns.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 32% YoY; caustic volumes +2%, ECUs -4%. PBDIT flat at INR163 crore, held back by fixed costs from expansion, including a one-time INR19 crore government incentive. ECH plant fully commissioned in April 2026, running at 60-70% utilisation.

segments.name: Vinyl
segments.commentary: Revenue up 19% YoY, with PVC volumes +23% and carbide +5%. PBDIT rose 68% to INR39 crore on higher prices, lower energy costs and better efficiency. PVC prices are volatile, currently around INR81-82/kg per management.

segments.name: Sugar and ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue down 3% to INR991 crore; ethanol prices -15% on sales mix. PBDIT down 18% to INR207 crore as cane prices rose 8%. Crush fell to 473 lakh quintals with recovery of 10.8%; sugar inventory 32.2 lakh quintals vs 39.9 lakh a year ago.

segments.name: Fenesta Building Systems
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,112 crore (+28%). Q4 revenue +34% YoY, but PBDIT up only 6% to INR37 crore given fixed costs and new platforms. Order book up 15%.

segments.name: Shriram Farm Solutions
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth in FY26; research wheat sales +22% to a record. Q4 revenue +32% YoY in an off-season quarter. 13 new products launched in FY26, four from in-house R&D.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue down 11% on a maintenance shutdown. Outstanding subsidy INR189 crore vs INR161 crore last year. Gas supply risk from the West Asia conflict flagged.

segments.name: Bioseed
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue down 1% and PBDIT loss of INR8 crore. Management said the FY26 cotton seed environment was challenging; kharif placements are reasonable, with cotton inventory a concern.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR1,000-1,200 crore, including board-approved projects and pipeline.
INR217 crore capex for ~48 MW additional renewable power for Bharuch, taking RE provision from 50.4 MW to 98.4 MW; completion around Q1 FY28.
INR101 crore capex to expand formulated resins capacity by 36 KTPA to 50 KTPA; commissioning by Q2 FY28.
Management expects Epoxy/advanced materials unit to reach break-even in FY27 and be slightly better than break-even this year.
Management expects sugar margins to shrink versus last year but the shrinkage to be not significant, with prices expected to improve from record-low inventory.
Management expects caustic capacity utilisation to stay robust in FY27 and reasonable margins in ECH if raw material and product prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Pujan Shah (Molecule Ventures): outlook for PVC pricing given China property weakness and possible closures of inefficient Chinese PVC plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Shriram said pricing is very volatile and hard to forecast; hoped the rupee depreciation supports import parity and that the 11% import duty returns from 1 July 2026. Current PVC prices around INR81-82/kg; China capacity is so large that closures cannot be verified.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj (360 ONE): when will MIP be in place and is there accelerated Chinese dumping or domestic inventory build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MIP is under dialogue with government, which has recommended a price considered too low; industry is pressing for a realistic MIP. China was ~50% of India's PVC imports last year, and no timeline can be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj: how will Middle East alumina capacity outages affect the global caustic balance and domestic pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Shriram said regional balances matter and the impact of one demand region cannot be directly correlated to price; expects robust Indian demand long term with some short-term volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha (Unifi Capital): ECH utilisation and margin outlook, and epoxy break-even timing?
qa_highlights.answer: ECH running at 60-70% utilisation, ramp-up over one to two quarters; management expects healthy ECH margins if raw material and product prices hold. Epoxy/advanced materials expected to reach break-even in FY27, with Amit Agarwal saying slightly better than break-even this year.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: is ECH margin still in the 20-25% range and will chemicals EBITDA margin (about 20% in FY26) improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said Bharuch should be assessed as an integrated complex; complex revenue +38% and EBITDA +50% last year; new products rose from ~14% to ~34-35% of revenue. Aditya Shriram declined to give a margin number.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: will sugar margins be material in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said margins are lower than last year, but record-low industry inventory (~4 million tonnes) should lift prices; shrinkage expected but not significant. The export ban has only short-term sentiment impact.

qa_highlights.question: Riya Mehta (Aequitas): Fenesta cost pass-through, margins and demand after aluminium price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said retail customers are hard to pass cost to, while institutional contracts pass through costs beyond a tolerance level; margin is hit until then. Demand is good with a record order book.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: FY27 capex and Bioseed kharif trends?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR1,000-1,200 crore including board-approved projects and pipeline. Kharif placements are reasonable, with El Nino risk and cotton inventory as the main concern.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR1,000-1,200 crore, covering board-approved normal capex plus some pipeline projects; management said 'currently committed is to that range'.
INR217 crore board-approved for ~48 MW additional renewable power for Bharuch, taking RE provision from 50.4 MW to 98.4 MW; completion indicated around Q1 FY28.
INR101 crore board-approved to expand epoxy-led formulated resins capacity by 36 KTPA to 50 KTPA; commissioning by Q2 FY28.

ECH plant fully commissioned in April 2026, running at close to 60-70% utilisation with steady ramp-up expected over the next one to two quarters; ECH capacity 150 TPD (~52,000 tpa), with 70-75% expected to be sold externally.
Kota 68 MW green power project: average supply 34 MW; average injection of 15 MW from May 2026. Aluminium extrusion project at Kota progressing on schedule (Fenesta).
Epoxy/advanced materials (acquired Hindustan Specialty Chemicals, completed August 2025) running at capacity; formulated resin capacity expanding from 14,000 tpa to 50,000 tpa.
demand_pricing: Chemicals: revenue +32% YoY; caustic volumes +2%, ECUs -4%. Management cites India caustic utilisation ~85% and domestic demand growth ~5%; India caustic exports ~12% of own capacity. Current lye ECU INR32,000-33,000/MT (excluding flakes).

Vinyl: revenue +19% YoY; PVC volumes +23%, carbide +5%. PBDIT +68% to INR39 crore on higher prices, lower energy costs. PVC realisations about INR81-82/kg currently; prices very volatile after China dumping, import duty waiver to end-June 2026, and West Asia-driven spikes. Industry seeking MIP and ADD; government import duty of 11% expected to be reinstated from 1 July if not extended.

Sugar and ethanol: revenue -3% to INR991 crore; ethanol prices -15% on sales mix, volumes flat. PBDIT -18% to INR207 crore; cane price +8%. Crush 473 lakh quintals, recovery 10.8%. Sugar inventory 32.2 lakh quintals vs 39.9 lakh; valued at INR3,876/quintal. Ethanol: OMC allocations ~1,100 crore litres vs ~1,900 crore litres capacity; cane-based share only 28%.

Fenesta: FY26 revenue INR1,112 crore (+28%); Q4 revenue +34% on higher prices and project volumes; PBDIT +6% to INR37 crore; order book +15%, management called it a record. Institutional contracts have cost pass-through beyond a tolerance band; retail is harder to pass through.
Shriram Farm Solutions: double-digit FY26 growth; research wheat record sales, +22%; Q4 revenue +32% in off-season; 13 new products launched in FY26, four from in-house R&D.

Fertilizer: Q4 revenue -11% on maintenance shutdown; PBDIT INR28 crore including INR33 crore one-time retention price gain; outstanding subsidy INR189 crore vs INR161 crore; West Asia-linked gas supply risk.
Bioseed: Q4 revenue -1%, PBDIT -INR8 crore. Kharif placements described as reasonable, but cotton carries high producer inventory and discount concerns; El Nino a concern for the season.
risks_watch: PVC price volatility from Chinese dumping and the 1 July 2026 end of the 11% import duty waiver; MIP and ADD outcomes still pending with government.
Ethanol allocation: OMC allocations ~1,100 crore litres vs ~1,900 crore litres capacity, with cane-based share at 28%; sugar margins to shrink.
Gas supply and LNG disruption from the West Asia conflict affecting fertilizer and chemical operations; subsidy receivables rising to INR189 crore.
Chemicals margin pressure from fixed costs of new capacity; Q4 PBDIT boosted by one-time gains of INR19 crore (Chemicals) and INR33 crore (Fertilizer).
Bioseed cotton inventory overhang and El Nino risk for kharif; Fenesta margin dilution from aluminium cost pass-through lag.
Next quarter: ECH utilisation ramp, epoxy break-even, PVC realisations versus INR81-82/kg, and sugar realisations.
key_quotes: So I think it i s very difficult to give an indication of what will be the prices going forward.
We are now exceptionally well positioned to explore synergistic value chain integrations across our broader manufacturing portfolio.
So we do expect that, you know, in case the raw materials and the finished good prices are reasonable, that we will make reasonable margins.

So that should be in the range of around INR1,000-INR1,200 crore including the normal capex as of now, which has been let us say approved by the board, but we have few projects in the pipeline as well.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term chemicals capacity, balance sheet and order book, but notably cautious and non-committal on PVC and caustic pricing, ethanol policy and margins, repeatedly citing uncertainty from the West Asia conflict and Chinese dumping. Management declined to give numeric margin guidance for ECH or chemicals.

adds.what: ECH plant (150 TPD, ~52,000 tpa), fully commissioned April 2026, ramping to 60-70% utilisation
~48 MW additional renewable power for Bharuch (RE provision 50.4 MW to 98.4 MW)
Formulated resins capacity expansion 36 KTPA to 50 KTPA (epoxy-led, Hindustan Specialty Chemicals)

growth.why: No company-wide revenue growth guidance; FY27 capex guided at INR1,000-1,200 crore with ECH ramp, resins expansion (to 50 KTPA, Q2 FY28) and RE capacity, while Q4 PBDIT fell ~6% (INR400 crore vs INR426 crore) on sugar cost pressure and management expects sugar margins to shrink modestly.
